quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What will protect your eyes from the wind?

options.text: Goggles
Windshield
Sunglasses
Eyeglasses

questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect a rider's eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not shield eyes well enough.

questions.question: Moving into another lane while turning is usually caused by:

options.text: Taking the turn too fast.
Lanes that are too narrow.
Not knowing how to steer.
Lanes that are too wide.

questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift into another lane or leave the road.

questions.question: Long rides in cold weather can cause all of the following, except:

options.text: Fatigue.
Hypothermia.
Severe chills.
Hot flashes.

questions.explanation: Cold weather riding can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from cold.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and allergy medicines usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you drowsy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most cold, headache, and allergy medicines make you drowsy and can hurt your ability to ride safely. Know how a medicine affects you before riding.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if the pass started before the zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the speed limit and only happen in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: If another driver is following you too closely, you should:

options.text: Not worry about them.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Speed up.
Get off the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up may only make them tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: To be more visible at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Turn your headlight off.
Ride with your headlight on.
Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Ride as close as possible to the vehicle ahead.

questions.explanation: Having your headlight on is the best way to be seen at an intersection. Your headlight should be on whenever your motorcycle is running.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Help you avoid traffic signals.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen, avoids wind blasts and other vehicles' blind spots, and avoids surface hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Lean as the operator leans.
Hold onto their seat.
Sit as far back on the bike as possible.
Never hold onto the operator.

questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean when the operator leans. They should sit forward without crowding the operator and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.explanation: You will seldom hear a flat tire. A sudden change in how the motorcycle handles is the main sign of tire failure.

questions.question: If it is warm outside, should you wear a leather jacket while riding?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are made to keep the rider cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are made to keep the rider cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket helps prevent dehydration and provides protection. Many jackets are designed to keep riders cool even when it is warm outside.

questions.question: In a normal turn:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.
The motorcycle should lean, but the rider should not.
The rider should lean, but the motorcycle should not.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean together.
questions.explanation: During a normal turn, the motorcycle and rider lean together at the same angle. In slow, tight turns, only the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright.

questions.question: If the front wheel locks, you should:

options.text: Continue to hold the brake and the skid should end.
Release the front brake and not use the front brake.
Release the front brake and then quickly squeeze the front brake.
Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the front brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately and re-apply the front brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: To be effective, an eye or face shield should be all of the following, except:

options.text: Free of scratches.
Resistant to penetration.
Able to fasten securely.
Airtight.

questions.explanation: Eye protection and face shields must be free of scratches, resist penetration, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to pass through, and fit over eyeglasses. They do not need to be airtight.

questions.question: A shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
Is only useful in protecting riders from dirt.
Does not offer as much protection as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also shields you from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles during normal riding.

questions.question: A thorough check of your motorcycle:

options.text: Is useless unless done by a mechanic.
Should not be done before a ride.
Should be done only after a ride.
Can help you identify any mechanical defects or equipment failures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help you identify any mechanical defects or equipment failures.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride. This helps you find mechanical problems or equipment failures that could be dangerous.

questions.question: When you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Weave among the three portions of the lane as the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases your crash risk. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, a horn:

options.text: Is useless.
Usually cannot be heard by others.
Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.
Should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used to get someone's attention quickly.
questions.explanation: Your horn can get someone's attention quickly. However, a motorcycle horn is not as loud as a car horn, so other drivers may not hear it. Never rely only on your horn to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: When making an ordinary stop, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use only the rear brake to save the front brake for special situations.
Use only the front brake to save the rear brake for special situations.
Sharply squeeze the front brake only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop. Using both brakes in everyday stops makes it easier to use both in a quick stop if needed.

questions.question: When braking, what should you do?

options.text: Use only one brake if it is not an emergency.
Use both brakes only on wet pavement.
Use both brakes every time.
Use only the front brake.

questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Stay in your lane.
Flash your lights to scare the animal.

questions.explanation: In traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving to avoid an animal can cause you to hit another vehicle, which is more dangerous. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting another car.

questions.question: How can you be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Make eye contact with other drivers.
Always use your headlight.
Wave your arms.
Ride close to vehicles in front of you.

questions.explanation: Use your headlight at intersections to be more visible. Position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space between you and other vehicles so you can move if needed. Do not count on eye contact alone to be seen by drivers.

questions.question: Which of these does not affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast a person drinks
Body weight
Height

questions.explanation: BAC is affected by how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Height does not affect BAC.

questions.question: If you are riding alongside another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. If another hazard appears, you may not have room to escape. Speed up or drop back to move away from the vehicle.
